relish._doc: Relish. hit_cue_s (D-d/E Step 4b): how long the hit cue holds after a blow: STRUCK -N with a jagged burst when it reached her hp (a warden's tell-attack, or anything once no undead stands), SOAKED with a smooth ring when an undead died in her place.

assist._doc: The warned-attack assist (an accessibility toggle, session memory only, no save field, no loot penalty): off by default. When on, every warned attack's tell window (warning shown to the hit landing) is multiplied by tell_mult: the Bellringer's slam rings and toll, the Huntsman's lunge, the Shieldwall's bash and rush lanes, the Pyre-priest's fire, Vei's weaves. Nothing else changes (damage, the attack beats, RNG). `enabled` is the switch's value at a session's first raid; the CONTROLS legend's LONGER WARNINGS row flips it (--raid-assist turns it on); a change applies from the next tell a warden lays, never inside a tell already showing (each warden keeps the length its running tell began with). tell_mult is at least 1 (a lower value is raised to 1). On, the first hit after a pack rest is placed a rest after the longer tell and rounded up to a whole beat (WardenLogic.after_rest), so it can land up to a beat later than off; a phase pull is not rounded (it is maxf(b + tell, last + period), off the beat on and off alike). Every later hit keeps the Pulse; off, nothing changes. In the short periods a warden has less time between tells (the Shieldwall turns only outside its tell).

sound._doc: The raid scene's sound warm-up (RaidSound.attach): these Synth kinds are rendered ahead of use, one render per frame from the scene's start, so no first play renders on a gameplay frame. A chime warms every score bucket and a streak every step (RaidSoundLogic.warm_plan).

danger._doc: Relish's danger read-outs (hp arc, screen-edge pulse, target mark). exposed_min and exposed_max: with no phylactery charge left, how exposed she reads (RaidLogic.exposed_level) runs from exposed_min at full hp to exposed_max at none; it drives the danger rim of her halo (dashes leaning to danger: at 0.6 already clearly red at full hp, since no revive is a state, not a mood). The PHYLACT. words are always danger with no charge left.

hud._doc: The stat block (top left). plate_alpha is its backing plate: near opaque so a corpse glyph or pickup under the block never crosses its text. Every HUD plate's alpha is pinned by tests/test_raid_clarity.gd: its dimmest text must stay 4.5:1 (lines 3:1) over the brightest thing the world can put under it, so lowering one fails the suite. warden_plate_alpha backs the awake warden's block.

stats._doc: The stat block's reading aids (RaidHud.StatBlock). detail_px is the size of its detail lines (the ESSENCE meaning and the PHYLACT. meaning; 13 or more) drawn in full text colour; label_alpha is how bright its row labels draw (text at this alpha; the contrast test measures it). ward_head heads the four rank rows (what the player owns); living_label and the enemy / enemies values (one '%d' each) say the LIVING row counts the dungeon's enemies, not people. essence_meaning, phyl_none, phyl_meaning_* and key_pile are the block's other words (RaidLogic.phylactery_word / phylactery_meaning).
stats.essence_meaning: circle it: RAISE undead · leave by an exit: BANK it
stats.phyl_none: NO REVIVE · a death ends the raid
stats.phyl_meaning_charged: a death here revives her in place, once
stats.phyl_meaning_none_1: revives Relish in place, at most once per dungeon.
stats.phyl_meaning_none_2: The Ossuary Tower crafts it from essence.
stats.key_pile: grey ×9 = a corpse pile (bodies in it): walk close, it gives essence

hint._doc: The bottom-centre hint (the idle, trance and exit lines, and the idle sub-line) on a ground plate fitted to its lines: plate_alpha backs it, bottom_px is the plate's gap above the screen bottom (the danger frame's inner edge is 10 px in, so at least 20), pad_px its side margin, gap_px the space between a line and the plate's edge and between the lines. font_px and sub_font_px are the hint's and the sub-line's sizes. The held door's prompt (door_prompt_h tall) sits door_gap_px over the plate's top. banner_plate_alpha backs the cue and wake banners, door_plate_alpha the held door's prompt. The words: trance_text, exit_text, idle_text, idle_sub_text (RaidLogic.hint_text / hint_sub_text).
hint.trance_text: DRAG A LOOP AROUND ESSENCE · each mote inside becomes one undead
hint.exit_text: AT EXIT · RETREAT banks your loot
hint.idle_text: HOLD SPACE · circle essence to RAISE undead
hint.idle_sub_text: your undead fight on their own · keep Relish safe and raise more

cues._doc: One-line onboarding cues shown through the banner. max_wait_s: a cue queued behind a visible banner is dropped after this many real seconds. first_mote_s: how long the first-mote cue shows. undead_s / undead_delay_s: the 'your undead fight on their own' cue's time and the scene seconds after which it is due even with no kill. first_mote_text / undead_text are the two cues' words.
cues.first_mote_text: ESSENCE IN YOUR SLOTS · circle it to RAISE undead · or carry it out an exit to BANK it
cues.undead_text: YOUR UNDEAD FIGHT ON THEIR OWN · keep Relish safe and raise more

legend._doc: The control legend (bottom left, above the trance meter): open every raid until a fort has been taken, then a collapsed chip the player can reopen. Sizes in px; plate_alpha backs it; chip_h is at least 44 (touch target).

retreat._doc: The retreat panel (RaidRetreatPanel): two columns, RETREAT NOW and IF RELISH FALLS. w is the plate's width; pad its inner margin; title_px/head_px/line_px the title, column-head and line sizes (no text under 13 px); line_h one line's pitch; col_gap the space between the columns; btn_w/btn_h/btn_gap the RETREAT and STAY buttons (btn_h is at least 44, a touch target). The words are RaidLogic.retreat_keep_lines / retreat_fall_lines; keep_prefix leads the left column's count line ('so far: '). head_* are the column heads; keep_all, keep_none, fort_yours, fort_vei and fall_revive the lines.
retreat.keep_all: You keep everything you found and all carried essence.
retreat.fort_vei: The fort stays Vei's · you can come back and break its warden.
retreat.fall_revive: a phylactery charge revives her here (at most once per dungeon)

goal._doc: The goal block (top centre, where the warden's block sits, before the wake and after the warden falls; a held raid keeps it the whole run): the goal line (goal_px), the route line (route_px) and the rows under them (row_px), on a ground plate at plate_alpha. The words are RaidLogic.goal_line / route_line and WardenLogic.break_line / takes_line / counter_line; the goal, route, no-army, rooms-seen and push-line (push_*, risk_*) words live in this block ('%s' / '%d' are filled by the code).
goal.goal_held: YOUR FORT · clear its counter-garrison for loot
goal.chest_row: open the chest to take the fort
goal.no_army: NO UNDEAD WITH YOU AND NOTHING TO RAISE · retreat, then send WAR here or bring big undead
goal.no_army_short: NO UNDEAD, NOTHING TO RAISE · retreat, then send WAR here or bring big undead
goal.route_here: you are in the warden's room

held._doc: The held-fort clear's banner words (RaidLogic.held_banner / held_payoff / held_map_effect): banner_text with no fort name, banner_holds with one ('%s' the fort), payoff the loot line ('%d' relics, remnants, essence) and payoff_husk its tail when the roll gave a husk, map_effect the counter-garrison mass this run killed ('%d').

gap_end._doc: A gap above idle.gap_s (the machine slept mid-raid) made the state end the run from its last checkpoint (run_ended, cause gap): the raid stops, shows the AWAY TOO LONG banner, and emits its one result beat_s later (a held beat so the banner can be read; the state ignores the result, the run is already ended). banner_s is how long the banner shows (past the beat: the scene is usually gone by then). banner_text is the raid's banner; banner_text_boss the Vei fight's (a boss run has no checkpoint: the state forfeits it, the party intact and Relish back at Vei's door, StateRuns.end_open), so it says the fight was called off.
gap_end.banner_text: AWAY TOO LONG · the raid ended at its last checkpoint
gap_end.banner_text_boss: AWAY TOO LONG · the fight with Vei was called off while you were away

vei_loss._doc: Every word of a lost Vei fight (BossLogic.loss_card, loss_cause, pressure_row, pressure_tag; vei_boss._lose and _lose_card; the HUD's BACKLOG row). ended: the loss card's line under VEI HOLDS, per end reason (ended_unknown for any other). banner: the banner as the fight is lost (banner_unknown likewise). The card's first row names the cause: relish_unmade reads KILLED BY from what struck Relish last (Relish.last_hit_src: killed_by.weave for her weave, killed_by.living for her guards, killed_by.other for anything else); horde_ferried reads BREAK (break_text: {best} her best streak, {need} the beats a break takes); fronts_held reads FRONTS (fronts_text: {fell} fronts that fell, {total}, {need} required; held_clause adds the ones that held, {held} their names from front_names, joined by join_comma and join_and). The next row is GUARDS, only when the break's pressure (VeiFronts.pressure_mult) is at least pressure_min: pressure_text ({mult} one decimal, {pool} her living pool, {reserve} the words after it, 'living in her reserve', the manager's ruling of 2026-11-18). tag is the short note after 'ferried X/s' in the HUD's BACKLOG row, under the same threshold ({mult}).

ended.fronts_held: her fronts held · too few fell in time
ended.horde_ferried: the horde was ferried · she did not break
ended.relish_unmade: Relish fell with no backup left

vei_loss.break_text: best streak {best} of {need} · the horde ran out first

death._doc: The death frame (RaidDeathCard): card_s is how long the death beat holds the card before the result goes out (the measuring bot never waits, it keeps the 0.9 s beat; 0 = no card), skip_after_s when a click or SPACE may end it early, fade_s its fade-in (none under reduced motion). The AFTER row's words (RaidLogic.death_next_row, read by the death card, the retreat panel's IF RELISH FALLS column and Vei's loss card): after_clone when a clone wakes her, after_unmade when she is unmade, after_in then the wait (' in 10 min') when the seed gives one, after_shock last for an unmade death (the town takes the morale shock). wait_* the AFTER wait's units ('%d' each). label_* are the card's row labels, cause_* / tell_* the KILLED BY and MISSED words ('%s' the warden's name), nothing / lost_bigs / shut_text the LOST, BANKED and SHUT IN texts.
death.title: RELISH FALLS
death.sub: THE RAID ENDS HERE, NOT THE GAME
death.foot: click or SPACE to go on
death.after_shock: · the town takes a morale shock

clear._doc: The clear card (RaidClearCard): when Relish opens the warden's chest the run holds one card naming what was won (the fort is yours, the warden broken, the loot, what comes next). card_s is the longest it holds before the win goes out, skip_after_s when a click or SPACE may end it early, fade_s its fade-in (none under reduced motion). The measuring bot never sees it (it keeps the wardens.victory_s banner beat). title ('%s' the fort), label_* and the taken / loot_none / next_text rows are its words (RaidLogic.clear_card_title / clear_card_rows).
clear.title: %s IS YOURS
clear.taken_text: its living become your dead · it joins your realm as a held fort
clear.next_text: Vei contests it once its grace runs out · send WAR there to hold it

loot_uses._doc: What each kind of loot is for (RaidLogic.loot_uses_line), read by the clear card's USE row and the retreat panel's dim line: relics, husk (a husk found: it wins over remnants), remnants, essence.
loot_uses.relics: relics are spent when you build
loot_uses.husk: husk: the frame a big undead is raised in · lay it on the crypt slab and slot remnants to shape it
loot_uses.remnants: remnants feed the crypt slab, which raises big undead

essence._doc: Essence motes and Relish's carried cluster. carry_orbit_px is the ring the carried motes sit on and COUNT on (12 clock slots, RaidLogic.carry_slot_angle); the drawing rocks the cluster by a sine at carry_spin_rad_s but never further than carry_swing_px from the counted slot, so a mote drawn inside a ring edge counts inside it. Reduced motion draws no swing. Draw only: no sim code reads it.

hound._doc: The Huntsman's hounds (wardens.archetypes.huntsman.pack): its own living, called at its hp gates; massless, they drop nothing.

ringer._doc: The Bellringer's ringers (wardens.archetypes.bellringer.pack): its own living, called at its hp gates; massless, they drop nothing.

bearer._doc: The Shieldwall's shield-bearers (wardens.archetypes.shieldwall.pack): its own living, slower and sturdier; massless, they drop nothing.

zealot._doc: The Pyre-priest's zealots (wardens.archetypes.pyre_priest.pack): its own living, called at its phase-3 gate; massless, they drop nothing.

tier_mix_by_fort._doc: D-d/E Step 4b: a fort listed here rolls its living's kinds from its own mix instead of tier_mix (RaidLogic.roll_enemy_kind; the same rng draws, so only the kinds change). For a fort whose composition, not its warden, makes the fight a grind. sable-hold (t4 Bellringer) and pale-bastion (t3 Shieldwall) lost their party bigs to brutes before the wake (sable-hold has one in its spawn room), and the warden's area attack then churned every re-raise for 300+ s; with fewer brutes the bigs mostly hold (seeds 1-6: 339 -> 157 s and 335 -> 151 s, D-d/E Step 4b).

enemy_room_mult_by_fort._doc: D-d/E Step 4c: a fort listed here scales the weight each room (by index) gets when its living are spread (LayoutLogic.populate_enemies: weight = distance from the spawn ^ 1.5, times this; the same rng draws). For a fort whose layout piles the living next to the opening. greywall (t1): its long room 1, the one room between the opening and the warden room, drew 12 of its 22 living; once the opening room was clear she met them alone at its door, they followed her back and wiped the 6-unit garrison by 13-15 s (8 of 14 died, ashgate and old-sluice 0 of 14). Half of room 1's weight goes to the warden room (seeds 1-19: room 1 x0.5 alone 4/19 died, x0.25 6/19, x0.25 with the warden room x3 6/19, this 1/19).

enemy_leash_by_fort._doc: D-e task 3: a fort listed here keeps the living of its listed rooms (by index, as enemy_room_mult_by_fort) in their own room until Relish first steps into it (RaidUnit.leash_hold; RaidLogic.leash_rooms / leash_holds). Held, they act like the detour's guard: they turn only on her undead inside their room, and follow no one out. Once she is in the room they are released for good. For a fort whose living leave a room the moment the army is seen and pile on her in another (greywall: the warden room's 12 gather in the long middle room). Absent or empty: no leash, byte-identical. Picked rooms [2] (the warden room) for greywall: frozen bot 0/19 and 0/20, typical human 3/20 (the pick rule asked 2/20; no candidate met both, this is the closest).

detour._doc: D-d/E Step 3, the guarded detour (LayoutLogic.detour_site / detour_guard, RaidPopulate): from min_tier up (never the first dungeon or a held fort) a cache lies in a side room off the path from the spawn to the warden room, bordering a path room (a normal room before a checkpoint, where loot would bank), cache_door_px in from the gap they share, and guard_by_tier of the fort's own living (the tier's mix, within guard_spread_px of it) stand on it: they come out of the fort's count, so the run has the same bodies, mass and motes, only placed. What it holds is loot.json cache. Fetching it is a push: the army has to win the guard's fight in a room off the way. The guard holds its post (RaidUnit.sentry, 3b): it turns only on what comes into its room and never follows out of it, so the fight happens at the cache and walking out ends it. 3c: the cache lies at the guard's post just inside the door (cache_door_px; LayoutLogic keeps it 40 px off the walls), so she takes it inside the guard fight, stepping through the door, rather than walking in to it after the fight. min_tier 3 (3c): at tier 2 even at the door the detour's walk kept travel over the baseline's share (6.0% against 5.3%), so tier 2 has no detour.

held_door._doc: D-e task 6, the held door (a set piece; LayoutLogic.held_door_site / held_door_walls, RaidHeldDoor; NOTES-RAID 'D-e task 6'). On a fort whose tier is in `tiers` (never the first dungeon, a held fort or the boss arena) one room on the route (a room on the shortest room path from the spawn to the warden room, not the warden's) gets a niche in one of its walls: niche_w_px along the wall by niche_d_px deep inside, behind wall_px walls, opening into the room through a door door_w_px wide. Where: of every wall stretch of every such room that keeps clear_px from each gap and exit and route_clear_px from the line the route walks through that room (each way in to each way out), the one whose doorstep adds the least walk to that line (the detour), then the lower room hop count, then the fixed side order n s w e, then the lower position. So the niche never pads: a decline walks the route as before, a take walks the detour. The cache (loot.json cache.relics_by_tier, the detour's) lies inside, within pickup reach of the doorway and out of reach through the closed door. A plate (plate_px square) lies beside the door in the room. The door is open only while a big undead stands within hold_px of the plate's centre; when Relish leaves the room (stands in any other room), the big sent to the plate is shut in behind the door: out of the fight, not in her party or ward, until the warden falls and the door unlocks (it rejoins). If the run ends any other way it is lost (party_lost; RaidLogic.held_door_lost, the one place the rule lives). How a big goes to the plate: Relish within order_px of the plate (her light's radius: she stands at the door) and a left click, the move click, on one of her party bigs sends that big; a click on the plate sends the nearest party big. There was no army order to reuse. Off: an empty `tiers`.
held_door._doc_geometry: The niche's points, in px from the door's centre along the wall and out from the room's wall: the doorstep (door_out) doorstep_px past the door's outer face (Relish's radius 13 and a margin); the plate plate_gap_px past the door's jamb along the wall and past the front wall's face; the cache cache_off_px along from the doorway's centre at the niche's mid-depth (in pickup reach of the doorway, out of it through the shut door: test_raid_logic raid_held_door); a shut-in big parks park_px in from the niche's far end (a big's radius 20 plus a margin); the zone checked against gaps and exits reaches zone_pad_px past the plate.
held_door._doc_words: The held door's words (RaidLogic.held_door_*; '%s' is the big's name): entry the world label and banner, prompt the plate's prompt, label_* the world label by state, row_* the HUD row, retreat_* the retreat panel's line (a leading newline; the panel drops it).
held_door.entry: HELD DOOR · a big on the plate holds it · it stays behind · the warden fight is harder without it
held_door.prompt: AT THE HELD DOOR · click a big to send it (the plate sends the nearest) · it stays shut in until the warden falls · a retreat or a death loses it
held_door.row_held: HELD DOOR · %s holds it · leaving the room shuts it in until the warden falls
held_door.row_shut: SHUT IN · %s · rejoins when the warden falls · a retreat or a death loses it
held_door.retreat_sent: %s is sent to the plate · lost if you retreat.
held_door.retreat_held: %s is on the plate · lost if you retreat.
held_door.retreat_shut: %s is shut in at the cache: a retreat loses it.

autopilot._doc_door: D-e task 6, the measuring bot's held-door rule (RaidAutopilot._door_tick / _door_decide, RaidLogic.held_door_pick; NOTES-RAID 'D-e task 6', frozen once written): decided once, at the first think she stands in the door's room before the wake, her read pause over and no living foe on her; take it when at least door_min_bigs party bigs stand and, once one is spent, one that meets the warden's weak point still stands (or none met it); spend the big lowest in the weak point's stat. Then: to the doorstep, the order (a click on that big) once she is within held_door.order_px of the plate with no foe on her, in through the doorway once the plate holds the door. She gives it up when the big falls first, or the door is not open door_wait_max_s after the order.

human._doc: The degraded bot (D-e, the human bracket; NOTES-RAID 'The degraded bot', under D-e): DEV knobs, all off unless given, that slow the frozen bot toward a player. --raid-autopilot-delay=<s> sets the one reaction delay (the warden tell's answer, the kite from the living and the no-army leave) and keeps the score's miss chance: delay and miss are decoupled. --raid-autopilot-read[=<s>]: on her first entry into each room (the spawn room included) she stands read_s scene seconds before acting: no move, no raise; the bot still sees and rolls every tell meanwhile, and a dodge off a tell she answers or a due kite ends the pause. 1.0 s is the low end of NOTES' 1-3 s per room: three or four fixations on a new part of the screen (about 0.25 s each) and a click; the rest of a player's room-entry hesitation (whether to push or wait) the bot's hold rule already spends. --raid-autopilot-draw[=<s>]: each raise opens the trance (ACTIVE, so its time is the split's trance) and she stands draw_s scene seconds before the circle is graded and raised (in the game Relish keeps walking to her last click through a trance; a player stops first, or the walk drags the carried motes out of the circle); a dodge off a tell she answers drops the circle (the trance's lockout, no raise: a traced left-drag is not a move click). The scene's time_scale stays 1.0: the bot measures scene time, and a player's slowed trance seconds are scene seconds all the same (RaidLogic.human_real_s converts). 0.7 s is a 2.0 s real circle at time_scale 0.35, the middle of NOTES' 1.5-2.5 s; the aim before opening the trance and a late start after READY run at full speed and are not in it. Capped at trance max_hold_s x time_scale (1.4 s), where a player's focus runs out. The bare flags take these values.

autopilot._doc: The reaction rule (raid_autopilot.gd _answers, one place for every warden): each warden tell is answered with chance 1 - react_miss, rolled once per tell from the bot's own reaction stream, and acted on react_delay_s scene seconds after the bot first sees it; until then, and all through a missed tell, she does what she would do with no tell. Both are linear in the target score between the react_score points (clamped outside). The kite from the living starts react_delay_s after a living foe in her room comes within kite_px (no miss: the living have no one-beat tell). Basis (NOTES-RAID, the bot's reaction model): a choice reaction to a visual cue is about 0.35-0.5 s in the lab (Hick-Hyman, two to four choices) plus 0.1-0.2 s for a cue at the screen's edge and a mouse move, so 0.6 / 0.45 / 0.3 s at score 50 / 70 / 90; against a one-beat (1.714 s) tell that leaves time to clear any of them, so misses are attention: a lapse of about 0.05 plus the share of fight time a player's eyes are on the circle (0.09-0.23 in the D-d/E pilot) times an assumed 0.7 of the tells that start during a trace going unanswered, 0.11-0.21, so 0.18 at score 70, 0.30 at 50 (longer traces, more redraws) and 0.08 at 90. DEV --raid-autopilot-answer-mult=<x> scales the answered chance (the context runs at 0.6 and 1.0). The Bellringer: the beat count says when to go in (the trip in and out fits before the tell with slam_safe_beats to spare), she works inside until she answers a tell, and a slam ring in flight sends her out. The Shieldwall fight (_vs_wall): while she answers a bash tell she keeps out of the bash arc grown by wall_margin_px of reach and wall_margin_deg each side, and otherwise waits wall_side_deg off its facing, wall_stand_px beyond that reach, walking round wall_step_deg at a time; she keeps her side until the other is wall_switch_deg nearer. The Pyre-priest fight (_vs_pyre): while she answers a fire tell she steps off a lit burn area that covers her (to burn_clear_px beyond its edge), first fetching a mote inside a lit area when the trip in and out fits before the beat with burn_safe_beats to spare; while acolytes live she waits pyre_stand_px beyond the nearest one (from the priest) and holds a raise until she is within pyre_raise_px of one (unless her carry is full, she is out of its room or a living foe is within kite_px), so the raised undead reach it; once it is exposed she waits pyre_exposed_px from it. The guarded detour (_detour_tick, D-d/E 3b, frozen from 3b on): she decides once, before the wake, at the first think the guard (or, with its guard down, the cache) is in view (a standing guard within detour_view_px of her) while no living foe is on her in her room. She takes it when her hp is at least detour_hp_frac of its most (detour_hp_frac_revive with a phylactery revive left) and her army is at least detour_army_mult times the guard she can see (RaidLogic.detour_take). On the way in she reassesses every think and turns back when her hp falls below detour_retreat_hp_frac (detour_retreat_hp_frac_revive with a revive) or her army below detour_retreat_army_mult times the guard still standing (RaidLogic.detour_retreat): early enough that a hit or two on the way out still leaves her standing, and the guard holds its post, so walking out ends the fight. Basis in NOTES-RAID (the detour rule). The unstick watch (_aim_at, D-d/E 3c): walking to a mote, pile or pickup, not closing on it by unstick_px of walking distance in unstick_s, she aims at the same spot pulled unstick_inset_px plus her radius inside its room; still not closing after another unstick_s, she gives that target up. The hold (stall_s) waits only on hostile foes in her room or the next: a calm foe out of the army's reach is no fight to wait out (D-d/E 3c). With no undead standing and nothing to raise from (fewer than min_motes carried or loose within collect_px, no unstirred pile within pile_px; RaidLogic.can_raise_from) she leaves after her reaction delay, as a player would, rather than after idle_s (D-d/E Step 4 review); the result's left_no_army says so.

party_profiles._doc: BALANCE 3's standard 'party of tier T' (DEV: --raid-profile=<T> --raid-fort=<fort_id>, RaidLogic.profile_seed): what the risk targets and the dungeon stand-ins assume the player brings to a fort. garrison_units are the player's undead already at the fort's walls (chaff at garrison.stat_mult); starter_units are the first dungeon's only (0 here); party is one big undead per entry, stats as the slab rolls them (the pre_vei fixture's four bigs run power 3.4-8.8, beef 1.7-5.5, speed 3.7-7.6). Each tier adds a big and grows the stats; tier 2's big just meets both weak points (beef 6 braces the Bellringer, speed 4 intercepts the Huntsman). The fort holds living = cap * profile_living_frac (the start's realm start_living_frac) and dead = cap * profile_dead_frac; no phylactery charge. Fixed before calibration: tune the dungeon to the party, not the party to the targets.

wardens._doc: The wardens (Bellringer, Huntsman, Shieldwall, Pyre-priest) and their fights. The meter row under a warden (warden.gd _draw_meter_row): meter_pips pips of meter_pip_px screen px, meter_gap_px under its body, and, while it is awake, the words meter_label at meter_label_px (13 or more) on a small ground plate meter_label_gap_px under the pips (so the row reads over the world); label_px is the in-world labels' size on screen; a dormant (unwoken) warden draws at dormant_alpha, and a Pyre-priest's sleeping acolytes at the fainter acolyte_dormant_alpha (their alpha is their only dormant cue).The Bellringer's clapper (warden_bellringer.gd): clapper_strike_rad is the strike angle, held clapper_hold_beats of a beat after a slam, and clapper_swing_rad_s the swing rate through the tell. The Shieldwall's GLANCE and FLANKED words hold shield_label_s scene seconds after the last such hit and sit shield_label_out_px beyond its body (clear of the crowd at it). The Pyre-priest's meter gives each acolyte pyre_pips_per_acolyte pips (the right-hand band, spent as they fall; its hp has the rest); its BURNED, SNUFFED and WARDED words hold pyre_label_s scene seconds. A warden's pack (archetypes.<id>.pack, the Huntsman's hounds) shows HORN and its entry rings through the horn, NAME · WARDED while it stands and NAME DOWN for pack_label_s after it falls, and THE PACK BREAKS · WARD DOWN for twice pack_label_s when it breaks because no undead stands (D-d/E 3c; the banner says it too). The risk lever (D-d/E Step 4; WardenLogic.spec): from lever_min_tier up, never in the first dungeon, attack_dmg_mult multiplies all of a warden's attack damage (dmg_unit to her undead and dmg_relish to Relish), relish_dmg_mult its damage to Relish only. Both 1.0: no change. A pack (D-d/E quality pass, knobs at their old values): its units come in at the horn points pushed pack_spawn_wall_px clear of the walls, and while it runs the next attack waits until attack.pack_rest_beats beats past the tell after the beat (the Bellringer, Shieldwall and Pyre-priest 1; the Huntsman 0, its lunge comes at the beat after the tell once the pack is down).

words._doc: The wardens' player-facing words, word for word as they were in the scripts (T2). Read with a blank fallback; a word with % keeps its placeholders (tests/test_raid_config.gd FORMATS). WardenLogic's pure helpers take this block (pack_teach, pack_label, shield_label, break_line, takes_line, counter_line, pyre_label, catch_label, pack_verb); the warden scripts read it through RaidWarden.wwords(). word_* are the one-blow kill verbs (the pack row, the draws over a Bellringer, Huntsman, Shieldwall and Pyre-priest). counter_make is the COUNTER row's advice tail: the compact row (the sleeping warden's ring under the goal block) is the same line built without it (counter_line compact := true). join_and and join_comma join the list of notches and gates; ord_* are the ordinal endings.
words.plate_foot: break it to take this fort
words.beaten_banner: THE WARDEN IS BEATEN · loot banked
words.pack_teach: at %s of its strength it calls %d %s · it is warded while they run%s
words.shield_line: front ±%d° glances ×%s · back ×%s · turns %d°/s · bash every %s beats
words.break_line: BREAK IT · your undead's blows take its %d pips, then open the chest it drops
words.takes_stunned: ×%s while stunned (an intercepted lunge stuns it)
words.counter_snuff: snuffs an acolyte in one blow
words.counter_make: : make one at the Crypt slab
words.catch_label: each catch costs Relish %d hp%s · it hunts faster at %s catches

relish_dmg_mult_by_tier._doc: D-d/E Step 4c: relish_dmg_mult per tier (WardenLogic.relish_mult; a tier not listed takes relish_dmg_mult). Read only where the lever is on (lever_min_tier up, never the first dungeon or Vei). Picked on seeds 1-19 at score 70 by the rule fixed before the runs (the value closer to 12.5% deaths; one death or less goes to 1.0): t2 1.0 12/57 vs 0.75 7/57; t3 1.0 15/57 vs 0.75 11/57; t4 1.0 3/57 vs 1.35 7/57. Graded on seeds 20-39. At 0.75 a 12 hp tell-attack takes 9 of her 30 (4 kill her; fire 6: 5), at 1.35 16.2 (2 kill; fire 10.8: 3).

wardens.last_chance: LAST CHANCE before the warden · your trance is ready: hold Space to slow time and circle · this raise costs no cooldown
wardens.last_chance_loose: · %d loose essence here: walk close to pick it up

presence._doc: A sleeping warden reads as a boss (warden.gd _draw_presence, dormant only): a plinth (flattened ellipse under the glyph, centre radius*plinth_y down, half-axes radius*plinth_rx by radius*plinth_ry, plinth_alpha), a boss ring of radius*ring_mult in ring_alpha with meter_n outward ticks tick_px long and a dashed second ring dash_gap_px outside it, and name plates (WARDEN, the name, and 'break it to take this fort') on ground at plate_alpha. name_px and label_px are the plates' text sizes and the _px knobs are all screen px (divided by the zoom). plate_gap_px is the clearance between the dashed ring and a plate.

bellringer._doc: The Bellringer (warden_bellringer.gd). The toll (D-d/E Step 4b): as a slam's tell begins, a ring attack.toll_radius_px wide lands where Relish stands in its room beyond the slam's reach, and only where an exit exists (WardenLogic.toll_exit, round 3): a point inside the room, her centre toll_exit_margin_px beyond both the toll's reach on her and the slam's, within reach of her spot in the lead less toll_react_s (a human's reaction, the score-50 delay) at her speed; sideways along the slam's edge counts. Else that slam tolls nothing (a corner the slam nearly fills, as lantern-keep s2). The bot's answer steps to that exit (TOLL; on every attack.toll_every-th slam tell, so the tells aimed at her per fight are near the other wardens'); on the slam it strikes her if she is still in it (TOLLED; a tell-attack, so the chain does not soak it), unless a beefy big braces the bell (MUFFLED: the counter spares her) or the slam's own ring will reach her there. Stepping out is the answer; it reaches the stand she keeps outside the ring, which the slam alone never did.
bellringer.name: The Bellringer
tells: slams ring out on the beat, and beef soaks them
rings faster at each third of its health

weak_point.label: a beefy big undead braced at the bell muffles its slams

pack._doc: D-d/E Step 3: the same pack as the Huntsman's hunt (see its pack _doc and WardenLogic.pack_*): from min_tier up, at each gate in at_hp_frac a horn horn_beats ahead calls size_by_tier of its own living (enemies.<kind>) into its room's far side from Relish; while any stands it takes ward_mult of every hit and holds its own attack; they drop nothing. 3b: a pack goes for her undead, not for Relish, and a big undead whose stat meets the warden's own weak point kills a pack unit in one blow (with the weak point's verb: MUFFLED, FLANKED, SNUFFED) and goes for the nearest while a pack stands; the army grinds the rest. The gates sit on its phase notches. 3c: a pack never goes for Relish: the moment no undead stands (or none stands as its horn sounds) it breaks and leaves the fight, dropping nothing (THE PACK BREAKS · WARD DOWN over the warden for pack_label_s, and the banner), its ward drops and the warden fights her alone with its own attacks, each answered by its counter. Sizes and ward_mult are Step 3's again.
pack.name: ringers

huntsman.name: The Huntsman
tells: stalks Relish and lunges on the beat
speed interceptors and the sacrifice chain counter it

weak_point.label: a fast big undead in its path intercepts the lunge

pack._doc: D-d/E Step 3, the hunt (WardenLogic.pack_*, RaidWarden._pack_step): from min_tier up (never in the first dungeon) at each hp gate in at_hp_frac it sounds a horn horn_beats ahead (on the beat; the entry points show) and calls size_by_tier of its hounds (enemies.<kind>) into its room's far side from Relish (the two inset corners farthest from her, spot_inset_px from the walls, spot_spread_px apart). While any hound runs it takes ward_mult of every hit (a stun's x2.5 multiplies with it) and does not lunge (one threat at a time); a full tell after the last falls it lunges again. Hounds are its own living: hostile at once, massless, and they drop no motes and no dings (a pack that fed the raises would shorten the fight it lengthens). 3b: a pack goes for her undead, not for Relish (it costs time and the army; her risk stays in the warden's own attacks), and a big undead whose stat meets the warden's weak point (here speed) kills a pack unit in one blow (INTERCEPTED) and goes for the nearest while a pack stands; its bodyguards strike the hounds that come in reach. 3c: a pack never goes for Relish: the moment no undead stands (or none stands as its horn sounds) it breaks and leaves the fight, dropping nothing (THE PACK BREAKS · WARD DOWN over the warden for pack_label_s, and the banner), its ward drops and the warden fights her alone with its own attacks, each answered by its counter. Sizes and ward_mult are Step 3's again. Step 4.1: its speed bigs leave the bodyguard post while the hounds run (it holds its lunge then) and hunt them (RaidWardenRun.guard_for); held at her side, they let the hounds wipe the army away from her.
pack.name: hounds

shieldwall._doc: The Shieldwall (warden_shieldwall.gd, WardenLogic.shield_*): stationary at its room's centre, it turns at turn_deg_s toward the densest crowd of undead within attack.face_reach_px (the flank-role undead left out; Relish when none is in reach; re-picked every face_repick_s), planted while a tell shows. A hit from inside its front arc (±front_half_deg of the facing, from the attacker's position) glances at attack.front_mult; from outside it lands (FLANKED; those pips are marked as the weak point's): in full from the side, at back_mult from inside the back arc (±back_half_deg round its back). Every period_beats it bashes its front arc, telegraphed tell_beats ahead (the arc lit): undead in it within reach_px take dmg_unit and are shoved shove_px away, Relish takes dmg_relish. Phases at hp thirds turn faster, widen the arc and bash sooner. Weak point: a big undead with wits >= threshold fighting it takes the flank role, walking round the orbit (its radius + the unit's + flank_gap_px, flank_step_deg at a time) to a post behind it (flankers spread flank_spread_deg apart), and strikes only off the shield. The rush (D-d/E 3b): as each bash tell starts, unless a wits flanker stands at its back (within its orbit + pin_px, off the shield: PINNED), the bash is a rush: its arc is rush_half_deg wider and rush_px longer for that tell and bash (RUSH over the lit arc), long enough to reach a conduit waiting at its side. Wits pin it; without them its bash is a threat to Relish as well as the army. The rush's reach is capped at rush_room_frac of the warden room's half-size (its shorter side; WardenLogic.rush_reach, D-d/E Step 4.1): in pale-bastion's 543 px room a 260 px rush covered nearly all of it, so an answered tell had nowhere to go (her rush hits: 9-13 a run there, under 1 at the-stair); the cap leaves her a ring to stand in beyond it (at 0.8 a conduit at her 223 px side stand is still within reach of her edge there) and changes nothing in a room 650 px across or wider. The aimed rush (D-d/E Step 4b): an unpinned rush turns to face Relish as its tell begins (when she is in its room) and lights a lane rush_lane_half_deg wide reaching rush_lane_over_px past where she stood (at most its room's farthest corner, WardenLogic.lane_reach): stepping out sideways or back beyond it are both answers; stepping out of the lane sideways is the answer, a pin spares her. rush_room_frac then does not apply (the lane is escaped sideways); it still caps a rush with her out of the room. The lane is also what the undead in it take. Round 3: from lever_min_tier (never the first dungeon) the pin is the rush's counter only; a pinned tell's plain bash still strikes her in its lit arc (below it a pinned bash spares her, as before). D-e task 4, a lever kept off for later (0; the manager counted a pin as the counter in reach instead, NOTES-RAID option A): from lever_min_tier, every rush_lane_every-th bash tell since the wake (counting every tell, pinned or not) is the aimed lane at her even when a wits flanker pins it (RUSH and PIN BROKEN over the wall, the posted flankers' rings dashed, the HUD line '· every Nth breaks the pin'; WardenLogic.lane_due), so a pin holds the rush off the other tells only; 0 is off. Why: a pinned tell's plain bash cannot reach the stand she keeps on its side (110 deg off, 223 px out, beyond its 140 px reach and +-80-100 deg arc), and 80% of tells were pinned, so 66% of the missed tells (55 of 83, seeds 20-39) were plain bashes she was not standing in. The lane's geometry (rush_lane_half_deg, rush_lane_over_px, the room's farthest corner) is unchanged, so every margin is too.
shieldwall.name: The Shieldwall
tells: its shield turns to your biggest crowd; blows on it glance
it bashes the lit arc on the beat; wits flank it from behind

weak_point.label: a wits big undead fights it from behind

pyre_priest._doc: The Pyre-priest (warden_pyre_priest.gd, warden_acolyte.gd, WardenLogic.pyre_* / burn_* / acolyte_*): stationary at its room's centre, with acolytes_base + acolytes_per_tier x tier acolytes (acolyte_hp, acolyte_radius_px) posted acolyte_ring_px behind it from the way in, spread over acolyte_arc_deg. While any acolyte lives it is warded: it takes ward_mult of every hit (phase 1, whatever its hp). Every period_beats it lights burn areas (burn_radius_px) tell_beats ahead and burns them on the beat: the phase's own `areas` on the densest essence or corpses within reach_px in its room (a pile weighs pile_weight motes; with nothing to burn, no area), plus areas_per_acolyte for each living acolyte beyond the first, aimed at Relish while she is in its room and reach (at most relish_areas_max: one on her, the others relish_spread_px round her). On the beat every loose mote inside is destroyed (BURNED -N; carried motes are safe), a corpse pile inside loses pile_burn_frac of its mass (burned away under pile_min_mass), undead inside take dmg_unit and Relish dmg_relish (each once per beat). Phase 2 when the last acolyte falls (exposed: no ward, sooner and wider fires), phase 3 at until_hp_frac. Weak point: a big undead with power >= threshold kills an acolyte in one blow (SNUFFED) and takes the acolyte-hunting role (it goes for the nearest living acolyte while it fights the priest). What the missing counter costs (the risk knobs): ward_mult and acolyte_hp (how long the fight drags without power), areas_per_acolyte, relish_areas_max, relish_spread_px and dmg_relish (the fire on Relish while acolytes live), dmg_unit and pile_burn_frac (the army and the essence it denies); the bot's autopilot.burn_step_off is how often a player steps off. relish_area_every (D-d/E Step 4b): on every relish_area_every-th burn beat one of its own fires goes on Relish (while she is in its reach), even with no acolyte left, so the fires aimed at her per fight are near the other wardens'; the acolytes' extra fires still fall with them.
pyre_priest.name: The Pyre-priest
tells: it burns the essence and corpses on the floor on the beat; step off the fire
its acolytes ward it and aim more fire at you; power snuffs them in one blow

weak_point.label: a power big undead snuffs an acolyte in one blow
